Please submit your answers by 1) updating this file in your GitHub repository and 2) uploading a .html file of the assignment to this repository. Please submit a link to the repository on Canvas. 

# Set up
1. Load the tidyverse library. 
```{r}
#install.packages("tidyverse")
library(tidyverse)

```

2. Load the billboard data. 
```{r}
install.packages("billboard")

library("billboard")
data("billboard")
```

3. Describe the dataset. 
```{r}
names(billboard)
summary(billboard)

#This dataset contains 79 columns (79 variables, including artist, track, date.entered, wk1-wk76) and 317 rows/observations. There are 228 unique artists in total with Jay-Z recorded the highest (= 2%) and 316 unique tracks in total. Date was recorded the time period of 1999-06-05 -- 2000-12-30 and the range of 2000-02-13 -- 2000-04-03 recorded the highest frequency with 49 (15.5%).
```

4. Print the column names from this dataset. 
```{r}
colnames(billboard)
```

5. Print the first 5 entries in the dataset. 
```{r}
head(billboard, 5)
```


# Practice
1. Create a subset of data that has Jay-Z as the only artist. How many songs are in it?
```{r}
jayz_data<- subset(billboard, billboard$artist == "Jay-Z")
jayz_data

#Answer: 5 songs
```

2. In the original dataset, use filter to find information about the song "All the small things." What was the highest position (i.e. lowest number) this song reached on the billboard 100? 
```{r}
info_about_allthesmallthings<- billboard%>%filter(track == "All The Small Things")
info_about_allthesmallthings

#Answer: 6 (week12)
```

3. Create a subset of data for songs Tim McGraw sang. Summarize the data for wk 1.
```{r}
McGraw_songs<- subset(billboard, billboard$artist == "McGraw, Tim")
McGraw_songs

summary(McGraw_songs$wk1)


```

4. Create a function that can be used to determine if Britney Spears sang the song. 
```{r}
detect_spearssong<- function(name){ifelse(name == "Spears, Britney", "Yes", "No")}
#detect_spearssong("Spears, Britney")

```

5. Test your function on the billboard data. Save the results to a new column called "wasItBritney"
```{r}
#detect_spearssong("Spears, Britney")

library(tidyverse) 
data("billboard")

billboard$wasItBritney<- NA
billboard$wasItBritney<- detect_spearssong(billboard$artist)
```

6. Use a for loop to determine if a song placed 50 or below or placed above 50 during the first week. 
```{r}
billboard$rank50orbelow_week1<- NA
for(i in 1:nrow(billboard)){billboard$rank50orbelow_week1[i]<- billboard$wk1[i]>=50}

#for(i in 1:nrow(billboard)){billboard$rank50orbelow_week1[i]<- billboard$wk1[i]>50 | billboard$wk1[i]==50}

This is the way I interpreted this question, please let me know if I'm wrong!

```

7. Use an if else statement to determine the same information as you obtained with the for loop. 
```{r}
billboard$rank50orbelow_week1_withifelse<- NA
billboard$rank50orbelow_week1_withifelse<- ifelse(billboard$wk1>=50, "TRUE", "FALSE")

```
